gst.notes: Default GST rate applied to most taxable supplies across Australia.

baseRateEntity.criteria: Aggregated turnover below $50 million and no more than 80% passive income.

failureToLodge.description: Failure to Lodge (FTL) penalties apply for late BAS and income tax returns. One penalty unit is charged for each 28 day period or part thereof that a document is overdue, up to a maximum of five units for small businesses.

generalInterestCharge.description: General Interest Charge (GIC) accrues on outstanding tax debts on a daily compounding basis. The rate is updated quarterly based on the 90-day bank bill rate plus a premium.

basQuarters.label: Q1 (Jul-Sep)
basQuarters.notes: Tax or BAS agents may receive an extension to 25 November.

basQuarters.label: Q2 (Oct-Dec)
basQuarters.notes: No extension even when lodging online; payment is also due 28 February.

basQuarters.label: Q3 (Jan-Mar)
basQuarters.notes: If the due date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.

basQuarters.label: Q4 (Apr-Jun)
basQuarters.notes: Finalise payroll and superannuation before lodging to keep PAYG withholding accurate.

annualObligations.name: Income tax return (self-lodged sole traders and small companies)
annualObligations.notes: Tax agents have their own lodgement program when engaged before 31 October.

annualObligations.name: Income tax return via registered tax agent
annualObligations.notes: Exact due date depends on your agent's ATO lodgement program listing.

annualObligations.name: Annual GST return (annual payers)
annualObligations.notes: Aligns with Q2 BAS deadline when you report annually.

annualObligations.name: Fringe benefits tax (FBT) annual return
annualObligations.notes: If lodged through a tax agent the due date can be extended to 25 June.

annualObligations.name: PAYG withholding annual report
annualObligations.notes: Electronic lodgers receive an extension to 14 September.

taxPlanning.disclaimer: General information only. Discuss with a registered tax professional before applying to your circumstances.

strategies.title: Smooth cash flow with PAYG instalments
strategies.summary: Review quarterly PAYG instalments so they better match your actual profitability.
actions: Compare each instalment with year-to-date profit and forecast the full-year result.
Submit a variation through Online services for business when income materially changes.
strategies.caution: Underestimating instalments can trigger interest or penalties if the variance is significant.

strategies.title: Plan deductions before 30 June
strategies.summary: Bring forward tax-deductible expenses or write-offs where it helps manage your taxable income.
actions: Review asset replacement plans and consider instant asset write-off thresholds.
Prepay eligible expenses (like rent or insurance) where cash flow allows.
strategies.caution: Ensure expenses are genuinely incurred for business purposes and keep supporting documentation.

strategies.title: Use superannuation contributions strategically
strategies.summary: Contribute to super within the concessional cap to reduce taxable profits and build retirement savings.
actions: Track the $27,500 concessional cap and consider catch-up amounts if eligible.
Ensure contributions clear the fund before 30 June to count for that financial year.
strategies.caution: Excess contributions can attract additional tax; check timing with your fund administrator.

strategies.title: Document business use percentages
strategies.summary: Maintain logs for mixed-use assets to substantiate the deductible business portion.
actions: Update vehicle logbooks every five years or when usage changes materially.
Record home office, phone, and internet usage with contemporaneous evidence.
strategies.caution: Private usage claims without evidence increase audit risk.
